topic.title: The IMAX seat is the film's real product
topic.claim: Ramayana's IMAX shows sell out first because people are paying for a story they can tell afterwards, not for a better film.
topic.behaviour: Audiences skip the regular screen and book the biggest screen for a big film, even at a higher ticket price. They post the seat or the screen, not the scenes.
topic.mechanism: A large film gets sold as an event, and an event needs a visible badge. IMAX is the badge, and the multiplex gets more per seat.
topic.group: Urban 24 to 32 year olds who book the 'right' screen for big releases
topic.moment: You open the booking app for a big film and your thumb goes straight to the IMAX show, even though the regular show is half empty.

turn.believed: People pay more for IMAX because the film looks better on it.
turn.actually: People pay more because the screen announces that they were there at the big moment.

topic.because: The cinema earns more per seat, and the film earns a bigger opening. You get something to post, so everybody is happy except your wallet.

proof.fact: IMAX is about 25% of Ramayana's advance collections from 3.8% of screenings, averaging about 170 tickets per show against 35 for regular shows.

topic.payoff: Test: would you still pick that screen if you could not tell anyone which one you sat in?
topic.send_to: The friend who books the premium show for every big release and calls it 'worth it'.
real_details: Premium recliner seats sold out in some Mumbai cinemas.
topic.news_peg: Ramayana: Part 1 advance booking numbers reported 26 October 2026, release 5 November.
topic.why_now: The film opens next week and the screen choice is being made right now.

score.why: People pay for the screen that says they were there. Reads as status, not a film review.
